source_caption:
When Richard Linklater and Glen Powell were casting the crucial role of Madison, they worried the character might devolve into a standard “damsel in distress” or a one-dimensional romantic foil. However, during Adria Arjona’s initial meeting with the co-writers, she actively rejected the traditional “femme fatale” trope. Instead, Arjona spent hours workshopping the character with them, injecting Madison with a desperate, survivalist edge and a deep unpredictability that constantly kept Powell’s character off-balance. This collaborative overhaul fundamentally reshaped Madison into a complex driver of the plot, directly setting the stage for the electric chemistry that anchors the film’s darker, twist-filled third act—including the flawlessly executed, tension-filled “Notes App” sequence.

Hit Man (2023), directed by Richard Linklater, starring Glen Powell, Adria Arjona, Austin Amelio, Retta. Based on a wild true story, a mild-mannered college professor moonlighting as a fake contract killer for the police department finds his meticulously constructed undercover identities unraveling when he falls for a desperate woman trying to have her abusive husband murdered.

source_details.synopsis: Hit Man is a 2023 American romantic crime comedy film produced and directed by Richard Linklater, who co-wrote the screenplay with Glen Powell. The film stars Powell, Adria Arjona, Austin Amelio, Retta, and Sanjay Rao. It follows an undercover New Orleans police contractor who poses as a reliable hitman as he tries to save a woman in need. The basic premise was based on the true story of a college professor who worked for the Houston police in the late 1980s and 1990s as a fake hitman, as described in a 2001 magazine article by Skip Hollandsworth.
